name: Ann Demeulemeester
founded: 1985, Antwerp, with Patrick Robyn. First Paris show 1991. She left the house in 2013.
founders: Ann Demeulemeester (born Ann Verhelst, 1959). Current creative director is Stefano Gallici — say so; the vintage that matters is hers, 1987–2013.
story: She is Antwerp Six. Pregnant and unable to travel to the 1986 London group show, she sent sunglasses; Barneys still ordered. The real origin is a record-shop window: at sixteen she saw Patti Smith’s Horses — white shirt, cuffs cut off, black ribbon. Years later she mailed Smith three white shirts she had made; Smith, then living quietly in Detroit, never forgot.

Smith has said that since she started performing again she has never gone onstage without wearing Ann. One S/S 1998 jacket became a Patti favorite, worn to death, and is now in the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame. PJ Harvey’s 2011 belt is the other end of that house.
style_codes: Elongated black tailoring, slashed and falling-off shirts, combat boots
Poetry printed on sleeves, androgynous déshabillé
Attitude: gothic without costume, rock without merch

quotes.text: I saw this record Horses and I didn’t know anything about it, but I went inside and bought it and put it on my turntable and as I listened, I thought, I have to know this person. I will know this person one day.

You can call it a corset, but it’s not, it’s a big belt I made… What I wanted to do with this was exactly the opposite of a corset… I wanted to make a shield or a kind of armor that would protect the fragility of a feminine body inside.
quotes.said_to: Vogue, Pitti Uomo retrospective, on the PJ Harvey belt
